difficulty_notes: Quantitatively heavier than a typical medium case (explicit NPV/weighted-average work and multi-year pilot modeling) but structurally fairly guided (clear framework, exhibits, and a focused pilot scope). Requires multi-step reasoning (region selection, financial modeling, implementation strategy, and risk assessment) but not the extreme ambiguity or data density of a top-tier MBB final-round case.

Short, well-scoped profitability case with explicit guidance and limited numerical work (market size given, few exhibits referenced). Some synthesis required around divest/repurpose decisions, but overall low ambiguity and beginner-friendly structure—comparable to the Easy calibration anchors.

This is highly ambiguous and synthesis-heavy: candidate must choose a firm, craft strategic changes, design a credible execution plan, quantify impacts on the fly, and defend risks with no exhibits. Math required is light, but the structural and execution demands closely mirror a tough MBB-style interview.

Moderate ambiguity: candidate must analyze a declining market, consider M&A and organic strategies, and stress-test risks. Math is straightforward (market-share and incremental-profit calculations) and exhibits appear simple, but the case requires multi-step synthesis across market, revenue, cost and strategy threads—typical of a first-round McKinsey case.

Low quantitative burden (straightforward market sizing and growth math) but high qualitative ambiguity and synthesis required around sustainability metrics, lifecycle analysis, competitive dynamics and consumer segments; overall a realistic mid-level MBB case. Exhibit complexity raises interpretation demands but does not make the math onerous.

Short, classic HBS practice growth case with low ambiguity and minimal math; primarily asks for application of standard frameworks (4Ps/4Cs/Porter) and a straightforward recommendation. Synthesis burden is modest (choose segment, entry mode, execution levers) and it feels more like a beginner-friendly prep case than a tough MBB interview.

Moderate difficulty: requires multi-step mental math (compounding price/volume growth and EBITDA projection) plus qualitative brainstorming to identify new revenue/EBITDA streams; ambiguity is limited by interviewer-led clarifications and the problem is typical of an MBB profitability/PE screening case.

Moderate difficulty: contains a multi-part structure (industry drivers, synergies, business fit) plus a bottom-up market sizing and a follow-on profitability analysis. Math is straightforward but there are multiple reasoning steps and some ambiguity around cost/price assumptions, making it comparable to a typical MBB Round‑1 case.

Requires multi-step BEFORE-vs-AFTER analysis (revenue loss, cost savings, TVM/working-capital impacts) plus a market-sizing and some NPV work; exhibits guide the candidate, reducing ambiguity somewhat but the quantitative and synthesis burden is still substantial.
